content_voiceover: This slide reviews treatment options for low risk MDS patients. The diagram on the left shows where each drug acts inside the cell. Luspatercept blocks TGF beta signaling at the cell surface. Lenalidomide acts on cdc25C, PP2A, and the CK1 alpha I K Z 1 complex, and is especially effective in patients with the 5 q deletion. Azacitidine, a hypomethylating agent, inhibits DNMT in the nucleus. Imetelstat inhibits telomerase. Deferasirox chelates iron and reduces reactive oxygen species generated from iron overload. Roxadustat inhibits the HIF prolyl hydroxylase enzyme, stabilizing hypoxia inducible factor to stimulate erythropoiesis. On the right, the clinical approach for low risk MDS is organized into three goals. First, maintaining quality of life through G dash C S F and transfusions. Second, avoiding iron deposition using deferasirox. Third, and importantly, improving anemia, using agents that are largely not covered by Taiwan's national health insurance, including E S A, luspatercept, hypomethylating agents, A T G or cyclosporine A as immunosuppressive therapy, lenalidomide specifically for chromosome 5 q deletion, and imetelstat. Finally, for improving platelet counts, T P O, meaning thrombopoietin receptor agonists, is used.
keypoints: Low risk MDS treatment has three goals: quality of life, avoiding iron overload, improving anemia
G dash C S F and transfusions support quality of life
Deferasirox chelates iron to prevent deposition and reduce reactive oxygen species
Anemia agents include E S A, luspatercept, H M A, A T G slash C s A, lenalidomide, and imetelstat
Lenalidomide is specifically effective for MDS with the 5 q deletion, and T P O agents help platelets
keypoint_voiceover: Focus on the three treatment goals for low risk MDS: quality of life with growth factor and transfusion, iron chelation with deferasirox, and anemia correction with an expanding drug list including E S A, luspatercept, hypomethylating agents, immunosuppression, and imetelstat. Remember that lenalidomide is the go to choice specifically when a 5 q deletion is present, and note that most of these anemia directed therapies are not reimbursed under national health insurance.
